calls.head: In close vs. From distance
calls.body: The Predators get in close, but the Sharks mostly shoot from distance. Nashville is one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and San Jose is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Predators to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Smith has a goal and two assists as the Sharks beat the Predators
paras: Will Smith and Collin Graf scored less than four minutes apart in the second half of the first to put the Sharks up 2-0. Ivar Stenberg stretched the lead to 3-0 early in the second, and that one stood up as the winner. Nils Höglander got the Predators on the board late in the period, and Macklin Celebrini made it 4-1 for the Sharks early in the third. Steven Stamkos cut San Jose’s lead to 4-2 on the power play with three and a half minutes left. Smith and Celebrini each had a goal and two assists.

The Sharks were outshot 34-24, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. The Predators hit three posts and still lost. Alex Nedeljkovic made 32 saves for the Sharks, and Juuse Saros stopped 20 of 24 at the other end. The Sharks improved to 10-11-2, fourth in the Pacific, while the Preds dropped to 11-5-5, slipping to third in the Central.
